title: Amazing Thailand Marathon Bangkok 2026 Review: What the 2025 Race Was Like
seo_title: Amazing Thailand Marathon Bangkok Review: Course, Weather, Crowds
meta_description: Amazing Thailand Marathon Bangkok review: a 2am start at MBK, 21°C and 73% humidity in 2025, 21 water stations, crowded late blocks, course records and 5,839 marathon finishers.
dek: What it was like to run Bangkok's biggest race in 2025: the point-to-point course from MBK over the Rama VIII Bridge to Sanam Luang, an unusually cool and dry night, the aid stations and cut-offs, and what went wrong with crowds, toilets, bags and shirts.
verdict: Enter if you want a big-city marathon through Bangkok's old town on a night start, with a fast front of the field and a seven-hour limit. In 2025, 5,839 runners finished the marathon, both course records fell, and the air at Don Mueang airport was 21°C with a dew point of 16°C at the 2am start: comfortable running air for a tropical city. The catch is the crowd. With about 48,000 entries, later start blocks were packed, toilets and baggage queues were criticised, and some finishers went without a finisher shirt. Leave plenty of time to reach the start, and carry a little water for the last few kilometres.

sections.heading: The Course: Point to Point Across the Old City
paragraphs: The marathon starts on Phaya Thai Road beside MBK Center and finishes at Sanam Luang, beside the Grand Palace. On the 2025 map it loops around Lumpini Park in the first 9 km, heads north to Victory Monument at 12.2 km and past the Ananta Samakhom Throne Hall at 17 km, and crosses the Rama VIII Bridge at 19 km. From about 22 km to 35 km it runs out and back along Borommaratchachonnani Road towards Taling Chan, turning at about 29 km, then recrosses the bridge at 38 km and finishes past the Golden Mountain at 40 km, Democracy Monument and the Grand Palace [1].

The half marathon starts with the marathon and follows its route for the first 16 km or so, past Victory Monument and the King Rama V Monument, then turns south past the Golden Mountain and Democracy Monument to the finish, skipping the bridge and the western out-and-back [2][3]. The organiser calls its courses fast and flat [4].

This route has only been used since 2024; from 2018 to 2023 the race ran from Rajamangala Stadium to Democracy Monument [3]. A Sports Authority of Thailand executive said the move was forced by work on the Orange Line subway and that a return to Rajamangala will be considered once it is finished [5]. One marathoner who also ran in 2024 said a small change after the start in 2025 improved the route [6].

sections.heading: The Weather: A Cool, Dry Night
paragraphs: Don Mueang airport, about 20 km north of the start and finish, recorded 21°C at 2am, with a dew point of 16°C, 73% humidity and a 4-knot wind [7]. It cooled to 20°C by 4am and stayed there until 7am, then warmed to 22°C at 8am, 24°C at 9am and 25°C at 9.30am, when the marathon closed, with humidity falling to 50% [7].

A dew point of 15°C to 16°C is comfortable running air: sweat evaporates freely, and the heat cost is small. With a median marathon time of 4 hours 54 minutes and a typical 15-minute wait to cross the start line [8], a typical marathoner finished at around 7.10am, when it was 20°C to 21°C [7]. Both course records fell that morning [3]. This is one night's reading, so check the forecast in race week before you set a pace.

sections.heading: Aid Stations and Cut-offs
paragraphs: The 2025 marathon map shows 21 water stations: every 2 km to 10 km, then at 12.2, 14, 16.5, 18, 20, 22, 25, 27, 29, 31, 33, 36, 38, 40 and 41 km and the finish, each with a medical point. There were bananas at 10, 18, 29 and 40 km and at the finish, and a sponsor's Hit The Wall station at 29 km [1]. The half had 11 stations [2].

In practice one marathoner said full-marathon runners had no water at 40 km: after the Rama VIII Bridge a fence separated them from the half-marathon lane, where the station was, so the last water they could reach was at 38.5 km. The same runner said the bottles were hard to open, and some women could not open them [6].

The listed cut-offs were 9.30am for the marathon, 6am for the half, 8.30am for the 10 km and 7.45am for the 4.5 km [9]. The organiser's 2026 rules explain the marathon limit: seven hours, counted from the last runner to cross the start at 2.30am [4]. In 2025 no marathon finisher is listed after 9.30am, but the results include 1,002 half-marathon finishers who crossed the line after 6am [8], so the half limit appears not to have been applied to the published results.

sections.heading: What Went Wrong: Crowds, Toilets, Bags and Shirts
paragraphs: With close to 48,000 entries, space was the main complaint. One marathoner said the early blocks could run freely but the later blocks filled the road, making passing hard [6], and the results show the median marathoner crossed the start line about 15 minutes after the gun and the last about 35 minutes after it [8]. A 10 km runner who took the MRT at 4.30am wrote that the train was full, that they underestimated how long it would take to reach the start, and that they still started right at the back [10].

The marathoner also said 10 km runners walked across the finishing straight before 6am to reach their own start, getting in the way of marathon finishers; that the city's toilet trucks by the start and finish could not be used; and that the baggage queue was very long because the bag trucks arrived late, with no signs to find them. They scored the race 7 out of 10, down from 9 the year before, while still running their best time since Covid [6].

After the race, runners criticised the finisher-shirt handout: staff did not mark bibs when shirts were collected, some runners went round twice and resold the extras, and many later finishers got none. The organiser took their names and promised to send shirts later [11]. Before the race, runners had complained that the race shirts ran 2 to 3 inches larger than the size chart [12].

Several men also raced on women's bibs they had bought and won women's age-group places; the organiser later re-ranked the categories [11], and the published results flag 14 entries as having run in the wrong gender category [8].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: Ethiopia's Agunafr Bekele won the marathon in 2:14:27, ahead of Tariku Abdi in 2:19:15 and Poland's Krzysztof Hadas in 2:19:24. Kenya's Eunice Muchiri won the women's race in 2:39:27, from Ethiopia's Hajer Kahsay Berhe in 2:43:49 and Meseret Yedaw in 2:47:55 [8]. Both winning times are the course records [3]. Prize money totalled 2,488,500 baht, with 227 age-group trophies [13].

The depth drops quickly. Tenth place was 2:30:55 for men and 3:01:10 for women, only 82 marathoners broke three hours and 1,164 broke four, and the median time was 4 hours 54 minutes. The half was won in 1:05:29 by Japan's Itsuki Yumoto and 1:21:03 by Ethiopia's Yanet Oli Erena, and the 10 km in 29:07 and 33:23 [8].
Queen Suthida started the marathon and half at 2am and ran the half beside Eliud Kipchoge, finishing in 2:26:40 [14].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: Registrations passed 48,000 within a week in 2025, and sign-up closed early [15]. Marathon entry cost 1,400 to 1,800 baht depending on when you entered, the half 1,300 to 1,700 and the 10 km 750 to 1,000, plus a 50-baht service fee. Race packs, with a Nike race shirt, were collected at Royal Paragon Hall in Siam Paragon from Thursday 27 to Saturday 29 November, and finishers received a medal and an e-certificate [9]; marathon and half finishers also got a finisher shirt [11].

Bangkok's governor said the BTS and MRT would run extended hours for race night [13]. The marathon and half started beside MBK Center, the 10 km and 4.5 km in front of the Supreme Court on Ratchadamnoen Nai Road, and every race finished at Sanam Luang, which served as the meeting point, food area and shuttle-bus stop [13]. The 2025 map directed marathon and half runners to the start from Siam BTS station, and 10 km and 4.5 km runners and finishers to Sanam Chai MRT station [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a night marathon through central Bangkok's landmarks with a big field, a seven-hour limit and a competitive front end. The 10 km and 4.5 km suit first-timers and visitors.
Think twice if you hate crowded roads or queues, or if you count on the cool air of 2025: one night's weather is not a guarantee.

The 2026 race changes shape. The half marathon moves to Saturday 28 November, starting at 4am from MBK Center with a three-and-a-half-hour limit. On Sunday 29 November the marathon starts at 2am, the 10 km at 6am and the 4.5 km at 6.45am, all from in front of the Supreme Court at Sanam Luang. The organiser says the split is for better management and that roads will be fully closed on both days. Marathon fees are again 1,400 to 1,800 baht, and race packs move to the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center from Thursday 26 November [4]. Check the 2026 route map before race day, since the marathon start has moved.

Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the official route maps, the organiser's 2026 race information, the full results, airport weather records, Thai and English press reports, an event listing, and two runners' own accounts.

faqs.question: What time does the Amazing Thailand Marathon Bangkok start?
faqs.answer: At 2am. In 2025 the marathon and half marathon started together beside MBK Center at 2am, and the 10 km and 4.5 km followed at 6.05am and 6.45am on Ratchadamnoen Nai Road. In 2026 the half moves to Saturday at 4am, while the Sunday marathon still starts at 2am, from Sanam Luang.

faqs.question: What was the weather like at the 2025 Amazing Thailand Marathon?
faqs.answer: Cool and dry for Bangkok. Don Mueang airport recorded 21°C, a dew point of 16°C and 73% humidity at the 2am start, and 20°C from 4am to 7am. It reached 25°C and 50% humidity by 9.30am, when the marathon closed. Both course records fell that morning.

faqs.question: What are the cut-off times at the Amazing Thailand Marathon Bangkok?
faqs.answer: In 2025 the marathon closed at 9.30am, seven hours from the last runner crossing the start at 2.30am. The half was listed at 6am, the 10 km at 8.30am and the 4.5 km at 7.45am. For 2026 the half has three and a half hours from its 4am Saturday start.

faqs.question: How many water stations does the Amazing Thailand Marathon have?
faqs.answer: The 2025 marathon map shows 21, every 2 km for the first 10 km and every 1.5 to 3 km after that, with bananas at 10, 18, 29 and 40 km. One runner said a fence kept marathoners from the 40 km station, so the last water they could reach was at 38.5 km.

faqs.question: How fast is the Amazing Thailand Marathon field?
faqs.answer: Fast at the front, thin behind it. In 2025 the winners ran 2:14:27 and 2:39:27, both course records, but tenth place was 2:30:55 for men and 3:01:10 for women. Only 82 of 5,839 marathon finishers broke three hours, and the median time was 4 hours 54 minutes.

faqs.question: How do you get to the Amazing Thailand Marathon start at 2am?
faqs.answer: By BTS or MRT, which ran extended hours for race night in 2025. The 2025 marathon and half started beside MBK Center, and the official map pointed runners to Siam BTS station. One 10 km runner found the MRT packed at 4.30am and reached the start late, so leave plenty of time.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-28 to the review template. Written about the previous edition (30 November 2025). Weather is from airport METAR observations at Don Mueang, not a forecast. The 2025 official website now redirects to the 2026 site and web archives were unavailable, so 2025 cut-offs and fees are from an event listing, cross-checked with the results; the route maps are the official 2025 maps as published by Thai PBS. Participant totals differ between sources (47,913 registered at the October press conference, over 48,000 per AIMS, 43,525 on Wikipedia); the press-conference figure and the results' own finisher counts are used. One Thai report names a Thai runner as women's half-marathon champion; the results show an Ethiopian winner overall, so the results are used. Runners involved in the bib incidents are not named. No rating.
